newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES, SPOTS CLOSE MOSTLY UP.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES, SPOTS CLOSE MOSTLY UP.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly higher on Thursday, boosted by the strong performance of domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 10.0 percent from 8.0 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover on the six-contract market rose to 1.36 million lots from 1.25 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Domestic share prices on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges rose sharply on the back of a surge in hard currency B shares, most of which hit the 10-percent limit-up level due to foreign buying, brokers said.
"Securities houses borrowed heavily on the repo market on Thursday due to the rise on the A share markets, pushing up both the repo rates and volume," a trader said.

Traders said fund demand on the repo market was also pushed up by one new A share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange on Friday, with institutions borrowing to prepare for bidding for the new shares.
Traders said the movement of the repo rates on Friday would depend on the performance of the A share markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly higher in active trading on institutional buying, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in July 2006 rose to 113.29 yuan from 113.08 yuan.
Combined volume on the eight-contract market soared to 1.6 million lots from 995,792 lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to continue to rise slightly on Friday due to firm market sentiment.
